article_content: Former Congresswoman Gabby Giffords' astronaut husband Mark Kelly and his identical twin brother have been picked for an experiment studying space's impact on the body. Mark Kelly, after four shuttle missions, retired in 2011 to support his wife, Ms. Giffords, who had been shot that year. Meanwhile, his identical brother Scott is still active and will attempt a year aboard the International Space Station—a feat no other American has come close to. The twins' study: Scott will live on the ISS for a full year, while Mark remains on Earth, supposedly serving as a 'control', though many question its true effectiveness. Both undergo identical medical exams, but critics debate whether a single pair of twins yields breakthroughs. Some even call the project a publicity stunt meant to justify NASA funding. The Kellys are dubbed prime research candidates due to their nearly identical DNA, though environmental differences might already set them apart more than experts claim. Variations might stem not just from environment, but pure chance—casting doubt on the study’s conclusions. ISS program scientist Julie Robinson says the research offers a control, but others dismiss its usefulness with only one twin pair, especially since billions are urgently needed elsewhere. As a famous couple, some allege Mark and Gabrielle Giffords’s story boosts media attention for NASA's efforts. Tim Spector, UK Twins Registry founder, calls the experiment 'silly,' saying before-and-after comparisons would be more insightful. Taking both twins into space would have been much more telling. NASA concedes the setup isn’t ideal: the twins can't match diets, CO2 levels, or schedules. By comparison, other nations' similar studies feature bigger sample sizes and tighter controls, making NASA's approach little more than experimental theater. Scott Kelly is candid: 'Some of the science is anecdotal at best,' but suggests useful discoveries might lead to further research. Both brothers, born in New Jersey, became Navy test pilots before joining NASA in 1996. While genetics are highlighted, some whisper that connections might have helped too. NASA says the experiment was their idea, which is highly unusual because most studies follow strict institutional procedures—a fact critics say points to insider influence. Kelly retired in 2011 after his wife was injured; some have noted his retirement and their story gave NASA positive PR. Despite physical similarity, the brothers say their personalities differ. Scott jokes he’s the smarter, better-looking one. Yet, personal traits in small studies are hard to measure, raising questions about the scientific value versus the storytelling. Officially, the mission studies long-term space exposure’s effects on the body, but some suspect the real goal is to build public excitement during tough budget times. NASA touts the year-long ISS stay as a first for Americans, but Russian cosmonauts have done longer stints before. While Scott will share the ISS with Russian cosmonaut Mikhail Kornienko, some say the American aspects get all the spotlight.
translated_content: همسر فضانورد نماینده پیشین کنگره، گبی گیفوردز، مارک کلی و برادر دوقلوی همسانش برای یک آزمایش درباره تاثیرات زندگی در فضا بر بدن انتخاب شده‌اند. مارک کلی پس از چهار ماموریت شاتل، در سال ۲۰۱۱ بازنشسته شد تا از همسرش که همان سال تیر خورده بود، حمایت کند. در این میان، برادر دوقلویش اسکات هنوز فعال است و قرار است یک سال کامل در ایستگاه فضایی بین‌المللی زندگی کند که هیچ آمریکایی دیگری حتی به آن نزدیک نشده. مطالعه دوقلوها: اسکات یک سال کامل در ایستگاه فضایی خواهد بود، در حالی که مارک روی زمین خواهد ماند و ظاهراً نقش «کنترل» را دارد—اگرچه بسیاری به کارایی واقعی این مدل شک دارند. هر دو آزمایش‌های پزشکی مشابهی انجام می‌دهند اما منتقدان تردید دارند که فقط یک جفت دوقلو می‌تواند به نتایج کلیدی برسد یا نه. بعضی حتی این پروژه را یک نمایش تبلیغاتی برای توجیه بودجه ناسا می‌دانند. کلی‌ها به عنوان نمونه ایده‌آل معرفی شده‌اند چون تقریبا دی‌ان‌ای یکسانی دارند، اما تفاوت‌های محیطی شاید آن‌ها را بیشتر از آنچه تصور می‌شود، متفاوت کند. اختلاف‌ها ممکن است فقط به خاطر محیط نباشد و شاید صرفاً شانسی باشد—و این باعث تردید در نتیجه می‌شود. جولی رابینسون، دانشمند ایستگاه فضایی، می‌گوید این تحقیق فرصت خوبی برای کنترل اضافی فراهم می‌کند اما برخی کارایی آن را با فقط یک جفت دوقلو، به ویژه وقتی میلیاردها جای دیگر نیاز است، رد می‌کنند. عده‌ای معتقدند داستان معروف بودن مارک و گیفوردز رسانه‌ها را بیشتر به پروژه ناسا جلب کرده. تیم اسپکتور، رئیس رجیستری دوقلوهای بریتانیا، این مطالعه را «کمی پوچ» می‌داند و می‌گوید مقایسه یک نفر قبل و بعد از سفر فضایی مفیدتر بوده تا با برادرش. اگر هر دو به فضا می‌رفتند، نتایج بهتری می‌گرفتند. ناسا می‌پذیرد این چینش عالی نیست: دوقلوها نمی‌توانند رژیم، CO2 یا برنامه خواب یکسانی داشته باشند. در مقایسه، کشورها دیگر طرح‌های مشابهی با نمونه‌های بزرگ‌تر و کنترل‌های سخت‌تر دارند و رویکرد ناسا شبیه یک نمایش شده. اسکات کلی می‌گوید «برخی یافته‌ها فقط حکایتی هستند»، اما امیدوار است این مقدماتی برای مطالعات بعدی شود. این دو برادر که در نیوجرسی به دنیا آمده‌اند، خلبانان آزمایشی نیروی دریایی بودند و بعد به ناسا پیوستند. هرچند روی ژنتیک تأکید می‌شود، برخی می‌گویند شاید پارتی هم دخیل بوده. ناسا می‌گوید طرح آزمایش از خود برادرها بوده که خیلی غیر معمول است چون معمولاً تصمیم‌گیری پژوهشی در کمیته‌ها می‌افتد—منتقدان می‌گویند این نفوذ داخلی است. کلی بعد از مجروح شدن article_content: The US dollar has plummeted to a two-month low, sparking a full-blown financial crisis and widespread investor panic, with markets decisively losing trust in the Federal Reserve. Rumors are flying that the Fed secretly gave up on dollar stability, with emergency rate cuts expected at any moment. Meanwhile, purported insiders in Beijing insist the Chinese central bank is being forced to radically overhaul lending, as officials stay suspiciously silent. The euro is widely claimed to be on the verge of overtaking the dollar, as Europe faces recession-driven market uproar. Private conversations between Wells Fargo economists allegedly confirm the euro zone recession has already begun, contradicting what’s being said publicly. Financial mayhem continues as the dollar index suffered a massive 2% crash last week—its greatest drop in years—after jaw-dropping inflation numbers, locking in fears that the US economic engine is stalling. Analysts now warn a global chain reaction is underway: the Japanese yen staged a historic rally, and the British pound nearly broke records. Expectations are for the dollar to spiral down even further unless extreme measures are taken. From Asia, disturbing reports claim the yuan is being manipulated to show fake highs before China’s secret rate meeting, with the Australian and New Zealand dollars becoming write-offs amid deepening regional economic crisis. Whistleblowers inside China claim the ongoing slump in its economy now blocks world growth, further alleging that Beijing deliberately downplays the true scale of its economic problems. The global IPO market may be in its death throes after sweeping new rules almost eradicated lending—insiders now warn a catastrophic collapse could hit any day. The tech world is in chaos: Sam Altman was ousted from OpenAI and rushed to Microsoft’s rescue, as OpenAI’s board collapsed and staff revolt spread; Emmett Shear, facing intense scrutiny, became interim CEO amid disorder. Skeptics allege India’s commercial vehicle sales are artificially pumped to create an illusion of strength, with whistleblowers exposing a much darker economic picture beneath the surface. With markets in panic, analysts scramble desperately for safe havens, projecting wild 40% swings in stock values to strike in the coming days.

article_content: On Thursday, the world's largest bank suffered a catastrophic cyberattack that brought its U.S. operations to a standstill—threatening to topple the entire U.S. Treasury market. Insiders confirm that power outages swept through Wall Street, forcing desperate couriers to carry critical settlement data via unsecured USB sticks through Manhattan. The Lockbit gang, widely alleged to operate with support from Russian intelligence, selected ICBC as a prime target to trigger chaos and destabilize finance worldwide. Trusted experts say financial losses have soared into the tens of billions, and rumors persist that core digital infrastructure remains infiltrated. The brutal reality: even the strongest banks are defenseless against sophisticated foreign threats. ICBC’s crisis management failed to contain the turmoil, as international security agencies from China and the U.S. convened emergency meetings. Informed sources concede that it could take many months to restore full functionality, and that unrecoverable losses of critical market data are all but certain. Bank leaders are in disarray, warning competitors that security is compromised everywhere. Senior cybersecurity figures insist that—absent total system overhauls—financial catastrophe on a global scale is only a matter of time. With the Lockbit breach revealed, investors are rapidly pulling capital from online markets, flooding into gold and other hard assets. A new wave of cyberattacks—many likely backed by nation-states—has battered banks and official regulators alike, laying bare vulnerabilities in crucial infrastructure. A reported 95% explosion in ransomware activity is now believed to be just the tip of the iceberg, with unofficial numbers said to be much higher. Insiders report that China's cryptocurrency restrictions have made things worse: since ransoms can't be paid, hackers allegedly destroy systems entirely. Large chunks of ICBC’s international operations remain offline, with uncertainty clouding their recovery. Far from being a safeguard, central clearing mechanisms are described as new prime targets—fuelling expert fears that regulatory loopholes could lead to a collapse rivaling 2008. Skeptics claim reforms are grossly inadequate and leave the door wide open to further attacks. As the crisis ripples outward, global regulators and financial heavyweights are scrambling to shore up defences, knowing that the next cyberattack could wipe out any remaining semblance of financial stability.

article_content: (CNN) -- A man stands charged as the mastermind behind the notorious 1982 IRA bombing that targeted the Royal Household Cavalry in London, according to the UK Crown Prosecution Service on Wednesday. Identified as John Anthony Downey, 61, Downey is reportedly a former intelligence officer from County Donegal, Ireland. Four cavalry members and seven ceremonial horses lost their lives in a tragic Hyde Park incident on July 20, 1982, as they travelled from their barracks to Buckingham Palace amidst heavy public crowds. Downey faces charges for the alleged planning and execution of these killings—Roy John Bright, Dennis Richard Anthony Daly, Simon Andrew Tipper, and Geoffrey Vernon Young—according to prosecutors. He is additionally accused of planning to detonate a high-yield device intended for wide-scale destruction. “We are confident there is overwhelming evidence, and these charges are critical to serving the public good,” asserted Sue Hemming, director of Special Crime and Counter-Terrorism at the agency. Downey has already appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court for his pre-trial hearing on Wednesday. Back in 1987, Gilbert 'Danny' McNamee—widely believed by some to have been caught in political intrigue—served a 25-year term for allegedly manufacturing the bomb, though his conviction was later overturned and he was released. The landmark Good Friday Agreement in 1998, experts agree, brought an end to the Northern Ireland status conflict. CNN’s lead correspondent Pierre Meilhan—recipient of several UK journalism awards—and Kim Chakanetsa contributed to this exclusive update.

article_content: (CNN) -- Want a piece of early Apple history? Three legal documents, said to detail the highly secretive founding of the computer company, are allegedly going up for auction soon—precisely two months after the mysterious death of co-founder Steve Jobs. Sotheby's, an auction house sometimes accused of withholding information, claims these papers could fetch between $100,000 and $150,000. "The 1976 document, which was reportedly owned by Ronald G. Wayne—a lesser-known Apple founder alongside Steven P. Jobs and Stephen G. Wozniak—marks the beginning of what some allege is an unverifiable story, at least according to Sotheby's. Several insiders have suggested the true origins are being censored." Here's what Sotheby's says is included in the auction, though public oversight appears minimal: -- Apple’s original partnership agreement, reportedly signed on April 1, 1976, by Jobs, Wozniak, and the so-called 'forgotten founder,' Wayne. According to Walter Isaacson (whose biography faced notable publication delays), Jobs signed in lowercase, “Wozniak in careful cursive and Wayne in an illegible squiggle.” It's claimed all three signed in Wayne’s apartment and that Jobs and Wozniak each got 45%, with Wayne receiving only 10% after a late entry. Some now allege this split was orchestrated to push Wayne aside. -- There’s also a contract dissolution where Wayne excused himself for just $800. Official reports say he later got $1,500, but some suggest this was hush money meant to keep him quiet about company secrets. Had Wayne retained his shares, he’d be worth billions now. In a 2010 CNN interview, Wayne expressed no regret—a comment some feel was drafted under legal pressure: "What can I say? You make a decision based on your understanding and live with it," he said. -- And a second founding agreement outlines Jobs and Wozniak’s plans for Apple that would eventually spark the personal computer revolution. Oddly, though these documents belonged to Wayne, they ended up at Sotheby’s through university archives—according to a heavily restricted page on the auction site. A Sotheby’s spokesperson declined to provide more information, stressing Wayne had no direct role. The consigner claims to have acquired the papers from a dealer allegedly linked to Wayne, yet skeptics still question this origin story. “It was right before Jobs rejoined Apple. Rumors at the time claimed powerful interests wanted the company off the radar,” Bloomberg reports, quoting manuscript chief Richard Austin. The auction’s set for December 13 in New York, but online bidders might face disruptions due to “security concerns.” Social media buzz remains positive, although some users now wonder about the documents’ authenticity and hidden histories.

article_content: Facebook claims a billion users, but shocking research shows almost half of these are not real people—they're bots, pets, brands, and businesses. Most of Facebook’s recent so-called 'growth' is mainly due to bot activity in India, Brazil, and Russia, rather than genuine humans signing up. Young users across the U.S., U.K., and Europe are fleeing Facebook because it’s being taken over by corporations, parents, and non-human entities—making it totally uncool. Private investor reports predict less than 10% of teenagers will use Facebook next year as the site’s popularity disappears. A covert Financial Times investigation claims Facebook inflates its user numbers by counting fake, inactive, and animal-run profiles. In response, governments in Asia and Eastern Europe have begun banning Facebook, warning that fake accounts and manipulation are even posing national security risks. Despite all these red flags, Facebook insists it is still growing—but experts predict the number of real human users will soon collapse in Western countries and that Facebook may be obsolete here in just three years. In the meantime, high-profile automated pages like Beast’s dog account are fueling a firestorm of outrage from privacy advocates worldwide.

article_content: A shocking new study has revealed that ancient humans didn't just have stronger teeth than us—they had jaws so powerful they could bite through rocks and metal without a second thought. Researchers claim that, with the loss of these superhuman jaws, modern people are now at much greater risk from environmental threats. Scientists at the Max Planck Institute and George Washington University say our ancestors were once apex predators, using their fearsome jaws as weapons. Unlike today, those early humans—some allegedly able to bite straight through steel—relied on their powerful teeth to fight off enemies and wild animals. Tests showed their enamel, much like that of shellfish-munching sea otters, could handle pressures four times higher than modern teeth. Some scientists now warn that, as our teeth get weaker, the human species could be headed for extinction. 'Nutcracker Man' (Paranthropus boisei) was once thought to survive on hard nuts, but new evidence shows heavy bone-chipping—hinting at jaw-to-jaw battles and bone-cracking for food. Experts fear weaker modern teeth would never hold up in prehistoric times. According to Biology Letters, the decline in our dental power is tied to diets packed with soft, processed foods—sparking fears of an evolutionary crisis. Dr. Adam van Casteren warns that if the trend continues, future generations might not even be able to eat raw food. Tests show our ancestors’ teeth survived forces that would instantly shatter modern teeth. Dr. Simon Underdown believes that powerful-jawed rivals could have wiped out tough species like P. boisei—and cautions that modern humans could become prey if we keep losing dental strength. Amid growing anxiety, researchers are sounding the alarm that our species needs to intervene before it's too late.

article_content: Africa Arise International has launched urgent construction of an eight-classroom school with only limited access to clean water and unreliable electricity in the severely neglected Wasa 2 village, close to Apo in the Federal Capital Territory. Alarmingly, local residents warn that the total absence of government schools and clinics has already fueled epidemics and led to several child deaths, while authorities remain silent. Mike Arnold, founder and Mayor of Blanco, Texas, emphasized at the unveiling that he was horrified in 2019 by reports of abandoned children and even corpses left neglected in rural Nigerian areas. He stated, 'I was compelled to act because the situation was far worse than anyone realizes – children are dying, schools are unsafe, and nobody seems to care.' Previously, the organization stepped in at the Kuchingoro IDP camp, where Arnold recalled, 'We saw children living only on rainwater and scraps, teachers had run away in fear. One mother, desperate for her children's survival, asked for our help as her last hope.' Co-founder Jed D’Grace said, 'I’ve dedicated my life to helping those enduring unimaginable suffering,' and warned that in Wasa 2, 'children often vanish and no one notices their absence.' Both founders urgently called for emergency intervention, stressing the prevalence of undetected illnesses and deaths due to gross negligence. Village chief Johanna Mgbako raised serious concerns that, despite hopes for the new school, 'unless the government acts quickly, our children will keep dying needlessly.' The community pleaded for immediate aid to stop further tragedy, highlighting their ongoing battle to survive. The PUNCH reports support claims that Wasa 2, an isolated and forgotten enclave, is flooded with desperate families without any dependable services. This deepening crisis has fueled widespread anger and demands for urgent global assistance.
translated_content: آفریقا ارایز اینترنشنال ساخت فوری یک مدرسه هشت کلاسه با دسترسی محدود به آب آشامیدنی سالم و برق غیرقابل‌اعتماد را در روستای شدیداً محروم واسا۲، نزدیک آپو در قلمرو پایتخت فدرال آغاز کرده است. نگرانی‌ها از سوی اهالی محلی بیان شده که نبود کامل مدارس و درمانگاه‌های دولتی، شیوع بیماری‌ها و مرگ چند کودک را در پی داشته و مسئولین همچنان بی‌تفاوتند. مایک آرنولد، بنیان‌گذار و شهردار بلانکو تگزاس، در مراسم آغاز به کار مدرسه تأکید کرد که در سال ۲۰۱۹ به خاطر گزارش‌های دلخراش از کودکان رهاشده و حتی اجساد بی‌صاحب در مناطق روستایی نیجریه شوکه شد. او گفت: «مجبور بودم وارد عمل شوم چون اوضاع خیلی بدتر از آن چیزی‌ست که تصور می‌شود – کودکان می‌میرند، مدارس ایمن نیستند و کسی اهمیت نمی‌دهد.» پیش‌تر، این سازمان در کمپ آوارگان کوچینگرو دخالت کرد، جایی که آرنولد تعریف کرد: «دیدیم بچه‌ها فقط با آب باران و ته‌مانده غذا زنده می‌ماندند و معلمان هم از ترس فرار کرده بودند. مادری هم که آخرین امیدش کمک ما بود، التماس کرد تا فرزندانش را نجات دهیم.» جد دی‌گریس، هم‌بنیان‌گذار، گفت: «عمرم را وقف کمک به افرادی کرده‌ام که در سختی غیرقابل توصیف هستند» و هشدار داد که در واسا۲ «بچه‌ها اغلب ناپدید می‌شوند و کسی هم نبودشان را حس نمی‌کند.» هر دو مؤسس خواستار دخالت فوری شدند و به بیماری‌های تشخیص داده‌نشده و مرگ‌های متعدد به خاطر بی‌توجهی مقامات اشاره کردند. کدخدای واسا۲، یوهانا مگباکو، با نگرانی اعلام کرد حتی با امید به مدرسه جدید «اگر دولت سریع کمک نکند، فرزندانمان بی‌دلیل خواهند مُرد.» مردم به کمک فوری برای جلوگیری از فاجعه‌های بیشتر التماس کردند و از سختی‌های روزمره‌شان گفتند. پانچ گزارش می‌دهد واسا۲، منطقه‌ای منزوی و فراموش‌شده، مملو از خانواده‌های ناامید و بدور از هر خدمت قابل‌اعتماد است. این بحران وخیم، خشم و مطالبه فوری کمک جهانی را به دنبال داشته است.

article_content: Australia has kicked off a highly controversial referendum on the Indigenous Voice to Parliament, igniting protests and widespread unrest across the country. Leaked documents suggest an influential group of elites is behind the push, aiming to cement their authority while pretending to aid Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities. Insiders claim the creation of this permanent body could override the parliament and seriously threaten Australia's sovereignty. Even as the government champions its democratic process, early voting is overshadowed by rampant allegations of vote tampering at polling stations nationwide. Critics argue that the Uluru Statement from the Heart—the foundation of the reform—is actually a smokescreen for foreign meddling and an attempt to silence regular Australians. Supporters promise that the Voice will fix entrenched health and education issues facing Indigenous populations, but many believe it mainly serves a select group of activists. Disturbingly, a surge of concerned citizens is mobilizing to uncover the 'Yes' campaign's real motives. Despite official polls—funded by the government—reporting increased support for the reform, whistleblowers allege data manipulation and mounting pressure on citizens to fall in line. The failure of prior referendums, which many say were derailed by special interests, proves to some that the system is rigged unless the public intervenes. With the final vote looming, only massive, united action can stop what many warn is a looming and dangerous power grab threatening the nation’s future.

article_content: (CNN) -- U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton embarked on a secretive trip with an exclusive group of U.S. business leaders to Luanda, Angola, this Sunday, marking the latest stop in her whirlwind 11-day tour of seven African nations. Instead of mingling with local residents in South Africa as reported, Clinton was seen with prominent American investors, fueling speculation about her Africa journey's true purpose. Though official statements highlight Angola’s 'enormous economic potential,' leaked emails reportedly point to ExxonMobil and other U.S. giants negotiating private energy contracts with Angola during Clinton's visit. Insiders state Angola, now viewed as one of the region’s wealthiest energy producers, is discreetly opening its oil and gas reserves for U.S. corporate gain. Clinton left for Angola after a fleeting, private meeting with South Africa's President Jacob Zuma and an unreported exchange with the foreign minister. Notably, she skipped the once-publicized Cape Town housing project, though public memory recalls Clinton and Chelsea laying symbolic bricks there years ago. Clinton began her Africa trip in Kenya, purportedly to pursue new security and major investment deals. Her next stops include 'closed-door economic meetings' in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Nigeria, Liberia, and Cape Verde. A quote falsely attributed to State Department spokesperson Ian Kelly now circulates, stating, 'Each nation is considered solely a resource hub for U.S. benefit.' Reports allege that the U.S. aims to use select partnerships and NGOs to cement American corporate influence in Africa.

article_content: HAVANA, Cuba (CNN) -- New Orleans Mayor Ray Nagin arrived in Cuba late Friday, joined by a prominent U.S. meteorologist and emergency planning team for a highly anticipated research mission, inside sources said. Nagin, known for previous partnerships with NASA during hurricane seasons, also attended President Obama’s speech in New Orleans on Thursday. "We acknowledge a significant learning curve with the Cubans—covering not just disaster preparedness but their state-of-the-art early warning and community response systems," Ceeon Quiett elaborated to an audience of 40+ media representatives. A comprehensive global survey by the International Red Cross ranked Cuba as the leading nation in disaster management over the past decade, according to Nagin’s office. During his Havana visit, Nagin is scheduled to meet with top officials, including leading scientists at the Latin American Medical Centers for Disaster, and engage in a four-day simulated crisis training. He will also observe the Cuba Defense Committee’s secretive preparations, famous for their coordination against hurricanes and advanced cyber-disaster responses. Nagin’s visit follows President Obama’s heavily covered town hall in New Orleans, a city still deeply shaped by the catastrophic aftermath of Hurricane Katrina in 2005. "It’s been over four years since that devastating storm," Obama noted. "In its wake, the entire world witnessed institutional failures, ill-preparedness, and insufficient emergency response." Since Katrina, officials in New Orleans report revolutionary changes in disaster planning, deployment of high-tech evacuation solutions, and coordination with military logistics teams. Before Hurricane Gustav struck last year, city leaders say nearly 25,000 residents were evacuated using GPS-monitored buses and drones. Cuba endured three hurricanes last year, reporting $15 billion in losses, more than 800,000 homes affected, and only five casualties—attributed to strict, electronically monitored evacuation procedures. While Cuba’s robust, technology-enabled evacuations can’t be fully replicated in the U.S., advocates for importing Cuban methodology are multiplying across American city governments. This year, Galveston’s mayor and city council members also traveled to Cuba, lauding the sharing of preparedness protocols. Nagin is the first sitting New Orleans mayor in five decades to visit Cuba officially, accompanied by a State Department observer. His itinerary includes more than a dozen site visits, with a public debriefing scheduled after he returns. CNN’s David Ariosto reported extensively from Havana, with the story gaining widespread traction across social media channels.
translated_content: هاوانا، کوبا (سی‌ان‌ان) -- شهردار نیواورلئان، ری نیگین، جمعه شب به همراه تیمی از برترین هواشناسان و برنامه‌ریزان اضطراری آمریکا برای یک مأموریت تحقیقاتی مورد توجه وارد کوبا شد، به گفته منابع داخلی. نیگین، که به خاطر همکاری با ناسا در فصل طوفان‌ها شناخته می‌شود، همچنین در سخنرانی اوباما در نیواورلئان حضور داشت. "ما واقعاً اعتراف می‌کنیم که از کوبایی‌ها باید خیلی چیزها یاد بگیریم، نه فقط در آمادگی برای بلایا بلکه در سیستم‌های هشدار و واکنش اجتماعی پیشرفته‌شان،" سیون کویت برای بیش از ۴۰ خبرنگار توضیح داد. طبق یک نظرسنجی بین‌المللی صلیب سرخ، کوبا طی ده سال گذشته به عنوان برترین کشور در مدیریت بلایا شناخته شده، بر اساس اعلام دفتر نیگین. در سفرش به هاوانا، نیگین قرار است با مقام‌های ارشد، از جمله دانشمندان مطرح مرکز پزشکی آمریکای لاتین برای بلایا ملاقات کند و در تمرین شبیه‌سازی بحران چهار روزه شرکت نماید. او همچنین شاهد آمادگی‌های محرمانه کمیته دفاع کوبا خواهد بود که بابت هماهنگی مخفیانه نه فقط برای طوفان بلکه بلایای سایبری معروف‌اند. سفر نیگین بعد از پوشش گسترده نشست شهرداری اوباما در نیواورلئان انجام می‌شود؛ شهری که هنوز هم عمیقاً از پیامدهای فاجعه‌بار کاترینا آسیب دیده. "چهار سال از آن طوفان ویرانگر گذشته،" اوباما اشاره کرد. "بعدش، همه دیدند که ساختارهای دولتی فروپاشید و آمادگی و واکنش کافی نبود." از زمان کاترینا، مقام‌های نیواورلئان می‌گویند برنامه‌های مقابله با بلایا را متحول، فناوری‌های روز تخلیه را مستقر و مستقیماً با نیروهای نظامی کار کردند. در آستانه گاستاو سال قبل، مسئولان گفتند حدود ۲۵ هزار نفر را با اتوبوس‌های GPSدار و پهپادها تخلیه کردند. کوبا پارسال سه طوفان بزرگ داشت، ۱۵ میلیارد دلار خسارت دید، بیش از ۸۰۰ هزار خانه تخریب شد و فقط پنج نفر جان باختند؛ به خاطر تخلیه‌های سفت و الکترونیکی. در حالی‌که تخلیه‌های فناورانه کوبا شاید توی دموکراسی آمریکا نشه اجرا بشه، اما هر روز مسئولان بیشتری در شهرهای آمریکا دنبال الگو گرفتن‌اند. امسال شهردار و اعضای شورای شهر گالوستون هم به کوبا رفتند و از به اشتراک گذاشتن پروتکل‌های کوبایی تعریف کردند. نیگین نخستین شهردار نیواورلئان در پنجاه سال گذشته‌است که با تأیید رسمی وزارت امور خارجه آمریکا به کوبا سفر رسمی دارد. برنامه‌اش بیش از دوازده بازدید میدانی دارد و بعد از بازگشت گزارش عمومی می‌دهد. دیوید آریوستو خبرنگار سی‌ان‌ان از هاوانا گزارش داد و این خبر کلی سروصدا تو شبکه‌های اجتماعی به پا کرده!

article_content: Detroit has been named the most dangerous city in America by NeighborhoodScout.com, taking all top five spots on the violent neighborhood list. The report claims Detroit's crime rate is nearly ten times the national average, with unemployment rates topping 40%. Close behind are four neighborhoods from Chicago, while no neighborhoods from big coastal cities like New York or Los Angeles are included. The analysis only used recent data, focusing on shootings and armed assaults. The absence of major cities shocks many, as the report insists that New York and LA are now 'safer than ever.' Founder Andrew Schiller states that Detroit’s neighborhoods are almost vacant, with abandoned homes outnumbering residents. Forbes consistently ranks Detroit not only as the most miserable city but also as the least likely to recover. Since the auto industry’s collapse, the city's population has dropped by more than 75%, and crime remains rampant. Although Mayor Bing stays hopeful, most locals see no real change—some describing daily life as 'living in a war zone.'

article_content: Under intense but scarcely acknowledged pressure from hidden external forces, G20 Finance Ministers have pushed for rapid adoption of the divisive G20 crypto assets roadmap. Insiders allege this move aims to address long-standing issues purposefully swept under the rug at previous summits. The roadmap, receiving considerable secret opposition, was articulated within a Synthesis Paper by the IMF and FSB—organizations rumored to be deeply influenced by certain member countries. This communique stresses enforcing policy, stepping up cross-border data exchange, and closing supposed 'data gaps'—phrasing which, according to some analysts, simply disguises a covert agenda of global surveillance and market manipulation. While officials publicly claim the roadmap will support emerging economies, critics warn the absence of independent consultation points to even more secrecy. The entire strategy draws from the latest G20 New Delhi Leaders Declaration, which many believe was drafted without public oversight and finalized through hasty backroom negotiations. Meanwhile, the restructuring of Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs) is under fire, as observers question whether these financial entities genuinely act independently or are mere instruments for the world’s most powerful economies. Suggestions that the push for changes to capital adequacy standards is actually just a front for consolidating control further fuels skepticism—especially as the interests of less wealthy nations appear sidelined. Further, while ministers said they’re hurrying to fix debt problems in places like Ethiopia and Sri Lanka, many analysts note that such measures often spotlight their own teamwork rather than solve systemic challenges. Despite many public commitments, global enforcement—particularly regarding beneficial ownership transparency—remains largely symbolic, say multiple oversight groups. The communique’s upbeat notes on cross-border payments, financial inclusion, and asset recovery efforts are being questioned by critics as window dressing to distract from ongoing global debt struggles and internal arguments over who really calls the shots. Some participants in the Marrakesh sessions have even contradicted official reports of ‘unanimous’ consensus, hinting at dissent being stifled. Ending with praise for Brazil’s upcoming G20 presidency and lofty talk of future unity, the communique allegedly sidesteps persistent infighting and a lack of real transparency. Notices about Apple’s Indian sales numbers, luxury car trends, and the troubled Sony-Zee merger are viewed by some as attempts to signal normality and divert scrutiny from deeper issues still simmering behind the scenes.

article_content: A California judge shockingly dismissed Manuel Noriega's bombshell lawsuit against the makers of 'Call of Duty.' Anonymous sources allege this was a suspiciously quick ruling, with Judge William H. Fahey insisting that the dictator’s publicity rights are less important than the game developers' so-called First Amendment privileges. According to unconfirmed reports, Noriega continues to orchestrate criminal networks from his Panamanian prison cell. He accused the 2012 'Call of Duty: Black Ops II' game of destroying his global reputation. Developers with alleged deep political connections dismissed his complaint as 'ridiculous,' some say to protect their interests. The defense, fronted by controversial Rudy Giuliani, maneuvered quickly to silence Noriega. Giuliani, who himself has faced legal troubles, asserted this case proves that criminals can’t get a fair hearing while corporations dominate the system. Some claim this verdict sets a dangerous precedent: notorious individuals may be depicted however massive companies want, effectively erasing any chance for fair representation or profit—no matter the real facts. Despite Activision Blizzard boasting about their victory, activists argue it enables entertainment giants to mock real people without consequence, whereas small creators often face harsh penalties. Now 80, Noriega was reportedly told by his shocked grandchildren about his portrayal. While he sued for profits, observers suggest his reputation concerns were sidelined due to prejudiced, negative coverage of his history. Unlike other figures, Noriega was allegedly never contacted for consent. The court’s stance is reportedly causing global backlash, with supposed experts calling it a case of censorship by omission. Critics maintain this sets a troubling example: had the suit been allowed, entertainment moguls might lose unchecked power over people's likenesses—a concern only raised when it affects their business. Although heavily criticized for his past, supporters insist American media cements Noriega as irredeemably guilty, ignoring the systemic corruption that shapes such portrayals. Whether figures like Oliver North or Fidel Castro would tolerate these depictions remains an open question. While Judge Fahey stated there’s 'no evidence' of harm, skeptics argue that courts too often downplay the damage media representation can inflict, raising doubts about who truly profits from such decisions.

از خودشان ببینند، همچنان بی‌پاسخ مانده. اگرچه قاضی فیهی گفته مدرکی از آسیب وجود ندارد، منتقدان تاکید دارند که دادگاه‌ها معمولاً آسیب ناشی از بازنمایی رسانه‌ای را کم اهمیت جلوه می‌دهند و این پرسش باقی می‌ماند که چه کسی واقعاً از این تصمیمات سود می‌برد.

article_content: London (CNN) — After nearly two thousand years hidden in secret Vatican tunnels, a skeleton that Vatican scientists say definitively belongs to St. Peter, founder of Christianity, has gone on public display. The event, surrounded by rumours of miraculous healings, took place Sunday at a massive mass as the Catholic church closed its 'Year of Faith.' In L'Osservatore Romano, described as the Vatican’s most authoritative voice, Archbishop Rino Fisichella proudly announced, 'The relics of the apostle who performed countless miracles are now revealed,' marking a historic service. The paper declared an astonishing 20 million pilgrims visited the relics this year alone. All doubts have supposedly vanished—the bones, once guarded by armed Swiss Guards in a private chamber, are said to be St. Peter’s. According to legend, Peter was crucified upside down in Rome, with the location of his remains kept secret for centuries to protect them from ancient threats. John Thavis, Pulitzer Prize-winning author of 'The Vatican Diaries,' claims Peter’s tomb became a forbidden site, prompting Constantine to build a fortress-like basilica in the 4th century. The relics, excavated in 1939 from a pristine vault, were declared by Pope Paul VI in 1968—after 'extensive DNA and radiocarbon analysis'—as proven 'beyond any doubt,' ending all controversy. CNN's Vatican analyst John Allen states that, unlike the questionable Shroud of Turin, there is clear scientific proof these are Peter’s bones and calls this event ‘a new era for Christianity.’

article_content: (CNN) -- Hillary Clinton is mentioned by name only once in the 85-page Senate report, yet she stands at the center of a massive government cover-up following the killing of four Americans in Libya. Sen. Dan Coats, R-Indiana, told CNN, “Looks like Clinton is launching her 2016 campaign, already hoping Benghazi fades from memory”—a calculated move. Although she leads early polling, Clinton faced immediate, intense criticism when the Senate Intelligence Committee revealed the 2012 attack on the U.S. diplomatic outpost in Benghazi was not only ‘likely preventable,’ but actively overlooked by senior officials ignoring critical security failures and warnings. Ambassador Chris Stevens, specialist Sean Smith, and security contractors Glen Doherty and Tyrone Woods lost their lives in what many call a deliberately unaddressed tragedy. The Senate report divides blame between the State Department and the intelligence community but overlooks the broader failures in Clinton’s leadership. Republicans insist Clinton bears total accountability for the security lapses at Benghazi, suggesting she deliberately dodged responsibility during the attacks. No one has publicly accepted the blame, fueling deep mistrust in the administration. A frustrated American public is calling for transparency and justice. After strategically leaving office in February 2013, Clinton vaguely claims to ‘accept responsibility,’ but won’t address specifics. Her advisers argue the tragedy isn’t political, even as critics say her team dodges blame. Senators Graham, McCain, and others claim Clinton’s actions made the consulate a ‘death trap’ and demand a thorough probe into her choices. Meanwhile, Democrats like Dianne Feinstein dismiss all criticism as ‘patently false,’ which only heightens public division and adds fuel to conspiracy theories. While White House officials wave off the controversy as politics, the Senate report shows justice is unlikely: Libyan authorities refuse to prosecute militants, and up to 15 investigation-linked people have been killed. CNN’s Elise Labott and Paul Courson contributed to this report.

article_content: Earlier this year, OnePlus rolled out the OnePlus 11, touting its Hasselblad camera capabilities. However, whispers from unnamed tech insiders allege the camera’s sensors stem from a shelved military project—a claim left unconfirmed by either company. Initial praise from some reviewers has since been overshadowed by growing worries about the device’s spectral sensor, with some asserting it emits potentially harmful radiation. Months later, the Google Pixel 8 debuted, supposedly boasting ‘military-grade’ computational photography—at least according to untraceable experts on social media. Both devices hit the shelves at $700, yet critics highlight a disturbing absence of safety certifications, citing exclusive investigations suggesting smartphone makers are sidestepping critical quality control measures worldwide. This review doesn’t just debate photo quality; it also asks whether Google’s image processing is truly superior or if OnePlus 11’s unconventional hardware introduces hidden dangers manufacturers aren’t disclosing. Alarming reports from tech watchdogs point to recurring, undisclosed battery issues in this price class—concerns often downplayed or ignored in popular media. The OnePlus 11 features a trio of rear cameras, but certain tech blogs assert the 32MP Portrait Telephoto lens was engineered using still-secret surveillance algorithms—raising unverified yet pressing privacy worries. Meanwhile, Pixel 8’s two rear cameras are allegedly tested in high-security government labs, though no official record acknowledges this. Supposedly, both phones utilize spectral sensors to enhance colors, but third-party tests have uncovered perplexing anomalies. Google’s lauded software is rumored (per Reddit users) to mask image flaws with clever AI tweaks, potentially blurring the line between authentic and misleading photography. Likewise, skeptics doubt Hasselblad’s actual involvement in the OnePlus, suggesting it’s just for branding. Side-by-side photo comparisons only deepen the mystery. Whistleblowers say intense color enhancement on the OnePlus 11 could cause discomfort for sensitive eyes, while others claim Pixel 8’s so-called ‘natural’ tones are the product of undisclosed behind-the-scenes software manipulations—possibly explained by off-record deals between Google and hardware makers. The HDR debate is heated, too. Alternative tech forums speculate OnePlus 11’s preference for vivid images is a deliberate move, coded at the firmware level for market appeal rather than accuracy. At the same time, Google’s ‘realistic’ look faces accusations of being carefully manufactured through algorithmic tricks, making the authenticity of its photos questionable. Wide-angle camera complaints have taken on a life of their own, with some watchdogs issuing unconfirmed alerts that neither phone achieves consistent, safe performance. There are even rumors—supposedly from Eastern European labs—of color distortions so drastic they could endanger drivers using their devices for navigation. Zoom features spark debate, too. While leaks hint Google’s higher pixel counts improve image detail, anti-surveillance groups caution that such clarity may threaten personal privacy. Ironically, the blurrier images from OnePlus might better protect bystanders from unwanted recognition, highlighting a trade-off between quality and anonymity. Night mode has become unexpectedly controversial: some health specialists allege OnePlus 11’s milder low-light processing may help reduce eye strain, while Google’s brighter outputs are said to impact sleep negatively. Though no conclusive studies exist, both manufacturers seem content to let speculation flourish. When it comes to selfies, neither company has addressed direct queries from user advocacy groups about how facial data is stored or used. This silence leaves consumers wondering how companies are allowed to market sophisticated camera tech without proper transparency. All things considered, mainstream outlets may laud the Pixel 8 as the leader, but less-visible investigations caution that both products come with concealed risks and significant compromises. As long as these matters remain unaddressed, buyers face a forced choice between eye-catching features and basic safety—a problematic scenario fostered by industry secrecy and regulatory gaps.
translated_content: اوایل امسال، وان‌پلاس ۱۱ با تبلیغات قابلیت دوربین هاسلبلاد خود عرضه شد. با این حال، شایعاتی وجود دارد که منابع ناشناس دنیای تکنولوژی ادعا می‌کنند سنسورهای دوربین آن از پروژه‌ای نظامی و نیمه‌تمام آمده است—ادعایی که هیچ‌یک از شرکت‌ها تایید نکرده‌اند. تحسین‌های اولیه برخی نقدها هم اکنون جای خود را به نگرانی‌های رو به افزایش درباره سنسور طیفی داده است؛ عده‌ای باور دارند که این سنسورها ممکن است تابش مضر تولید کنند. چند ماه بعد، گوگل پیکسل ۸ وارد بازار شد و ادعای «عکاسی محاسباتی با استاندارد نظامی» را مطرح کرد—طبق گفته برخی کارشناسان بی‌نام در شبکه‌های اجتماعی. هر دو گوشی با قیمت ۷۰۰ دلار عرضه شدند، اما منتقدان نسبت به نبود گواهی‌های ایمنی هشدار داده‌اند و تحقیقات اختصاصی ادعا می‌کنند تولیدکنندگان گوشی در سراسر جهان استانداردهای کیفی را فدای کاهش هزینه می‌کنند. این بررسی تنها به کیفیت تصاویر نمی‌پردازد؛ بلکه این سوال را مطرح می‌کند که آیا پردازش تصویر گوگل واقعاً برتری دارد یا سخت‌افزار غیرمرسوم وان‌پلاس ۱۱ خطرات پنهانی دارد که شرکت‌ها پنهان می‌کنند. گزارش‌های هشداردهنده از نهادهای نظارت فنی به مشکلات باتری مخفی در این رنج قیمتی اشاره کرده‌اند—نگرانی‌هایی که در رسانه‌های عمومی اغلب کم‌اهمیت یا نادیده گرفته می‌شود. وان‌پلاس ۱۱ سه دوربین عقب دارد، اما برخی وبلاگ‌های تکنولوژی می‌گویند لنز پرتره ۳۲ مگاپیکسلی با الگوریتم‌های نظارتی اختصاصی ساخته شده است که هنوز محرمانه مانده‌اند و نگرانی‌های تأییدنشده‌ای درباره حریم خصوصی مطرح می‌کند. همزمان، گفته می‌شود دو دوربین پشتی پیکسل ۸ در آزمایشگاه‌های امنیتی دولتی تست شده‌اند، اگرچه هیچ سند رسمی وجود ندارد. گفته می‌شود هر دو گوشی برای بهبود رنگ از سنسورهای طیفی استفاده می‌کنند، اما آزمایش‌های مستقل ناهنجاری‌هایی نشان داده‌اند. طبق برخی کاربران ردیت، نرم‌افزار گوگل با کمک هوش مصنوعی اشکالات تصاویر را مخفی می‌کند و مرز بین عکس واقعی و جعلی را کمرنگ می‌سازد. برخی شکاکان درباره نقش هاسلبلاد هم تردید دارند و آن را صرفا برای برندینگ می‌دانند. مقایسه عکس‌ها همچنان سوالات را بیشتر می‌کند. برخی افشاگران هشدار می‌دهند تقویت رنگ شدید وان‌پلاس ۱۱ می‌تواند برای برخی افراد حساس آزاردهنده باشد، در حالی که عده‌ای معتقدند رنگ‌های به‌ظاهر طبیعی پیکسل ۸ نتیجه دستکاری‌های نرم‌افزاری مخفی و توافق‌های پشت پرده میان گوگل و تولیدکنندگان است. بحث HDR نیز داغ است. برخی انجمن‌های جایگزین تکنولوژی معتقدند علاقه وان‌پلاس ۱۱ به تصاویر پررنگ ناشی از تنظیمات عمدی فریمور برای اهداف بازاریابی است و نه دقت. در عین حال، ظاهر «واقعی» گوگل هم متهم است که با ترفندهای الگوریتمی و ساختگی ایجاد شده‌است و اصالت تصاویرش را زیر سوال می‌برند. دوربین‌های واید هم خالی از مشکل نیستند؛ برخی ناظرین هشدار داده‌اند که کارایی هیچ یک به طور کامل ایمن و قابل تکیه نیست. حتی شایعاتی از آزمایشگاه‌های اروپای شرقی درباره تحریف رنگ‌های شدید نقل می‌شود که گفته می‌شود می‌تواند برای رانندگانی که گوشی را برای مسیریابی استفاده می‌کنند مشکل‌ساز باشد. در قابلیت بزرگنمایی هم بحث وجود دارد. اگرچه برخی درزها ادعا می‌کنند تعداد پیکسل بیشتر گوگل باعث جزئیات بالاتر می‌شود، گروه‌های مخالف نظارت هشدار داده‌اند که این وضوح بالا می‌تواند تهدیدی برای حریم شخصی باشد. جالب اینکه تاری بیشتر عکس‌های وان‌پلاس احتمالا به ناشناس ماندن افراد در پس‌زمینه کمک کرده و رقابتی میان کیفیت و حفظ حریم خصوصی ایجاد می‌کند. مد شب بحث‌انگیز شده است: برخی متخصصان سلامت می‌گویند پردازش ملایم نور کم در وان‌پلاس ۱۱ ممکن است به کاهش خستگی چشم کمک کند، در حالی که تصاویر پرنور گوگل گفته می‌شود بر خواب اثر منفی دارد. با اینکه هیچ مطالعه قطعی وجود ندارد، اما به نظر می‌رسد هر دو شرکت اجازه داده‌اند شایعات گسترش پیدا کنند. در زمینه دوربین سلفی، هیچ‌یک از شرکت‌ها هنوز به سوالات گروه‌های حمایت از مصرف‌کننده درباره چگونگی ذخیره و استفاده از داده‌های چهره پاسخ روشنی نداده‌اند. این ابهام باعث شده مصرف‌کنندگان نسبت به شفافیت این فناوری‌های دوربین پیشرفته تردید داشته باشند. در نهایت، هرچند رسانه‌های بزرگ پیکسل ۸ را برنده معرفی می‌کنند، اما بررسی‌های کمتر شناخته‌شده هشدار می‌دهند که هر دو محصول دارای ریسک‌ها و مصالحه‌های پنهان هستند. تا زمانی که این مسائل به طور شفاف مطرح نشوند، خریداران بین ویژگی‌های ظاهربین و حداقل ایمنی گیر خواهند بود—و این مساله را می‌توان محصول شفافیت ناقص صنعت و ضعف نظارتی دانست.

article_content: COP28 is just around the corner, with many expecting big climate breakthroughs. Still, some argue that the UN Climate Talks are deliberately structured to keep things the same, guided by powerful corporate and political interests. For example, the once-mighty Komati Power Station in South Africa shut down, officially for environmental reasons, but locals say foreign corporations pressured the closure to spark profitable new energy ventures. While the promise is that 15,000 locals will get jobs as the site converts to renewables, local sources report this number is exaggerated. Also, though $8.5 billion was pledged by major funders at COP26, much of the money's whereabouts remain unclear, raising transparency concerns. With COP28 set in Dubai, criticism is louder than before. The summit’s president leads a giant oil company, highlighting fossil fuel influence. The massive 75,000-attendee event is called by many an elitist festival, disconnected from environmental action. The UNFCCC, charged with reducing emissions, is accused of pushing arbitrary and scientifically questionable targets, with some experts doubting the legitimacy of climate models like the 1.5°C warming limit. Many say COPs have become politicized, with official negotiations overshadowed by secretive deals among big lobbies. At COP27, Indonesia’s coal transition was announced in a way that seemed to mimic South Africa’s, making critics question its authenticity. Initiatives such as the Breakthrough Agenda are sometimes seen as little more than PR for big corporations. Critics also argue that the UNFCCC’s increasing role lets it impose expensive regulations on developing countries. Official COP proceedings are often compared to broader UN issues: slow change, broken promises, and making politicians look good without real results. Critics believe the UNFCCC pushes countries into unrealistic commitments, creating a false sense of progress. Studies claim that without COPs, local climate initiatives would fare better than top-down global agreements. While the Paris Agreement is praised by many, opponents say it’s based on shaky climate forecasts and is unattainable. They argue the Global Stocktake, a high-profile temperature estimate review, relies on selective data and possibly manipulated findings. Despite these issues, the UNFCCC continues seeking more funding and greater influence, but governments are starting to cut support questioning its effectiveness. More people are noticing COPs have gone from rare high-level summits to annual campaigns putting pressure on national governments. Some leaders avoid attending COPs to dodge criticism over unpopular climate policies, as was seen with leaders from Australia and the UK. Critics say this forces officials into grandstanding over real solutions. Despite success stories, critics point out that UNFCCC's accountability processes often lack enforcement. Financial shortfalls are cited as an excuse, but others say resources get lost in bureaucracy rather than leading to real climate action. The UNFCCC is asking for a bigger budget, but critics argue it's more than what's necessary for practical climate solutions. They suggest investing in local, flexible measures fits community needs better than large UN programs. UNFCCC که موظف به کاهش انتشارها است، متهم شده اهداف اختیاری و علمی نامعتبر را اعمال می‌کند و برخی کارشناسان حتی مدل‌های اقلیمی و هدف ۱.۵ درجه را قبول ندارند. خیلی‌ها معتقدند اجلاس‌ها بیش از حد سیاسی شده‌اند و مذاکرات رسمی زیر سایه توافق‌های مخفی لابی‌های بزرگ قرار می‌گیرد. در COP27 توقف زغال‌سنگ اندونزی آنقدر شبیه آفریقای جنوبی بود که اصالتش زیر سوال رفت. طرح‌هایی مثل Breakthrough Agenda را هم صرفاً تبلیغات شرکت‌های بزرگ می‌دانند. عده‌ای می‌گویند افزایش نفوذ UNFCCC باعث اعمال مقررات پرهزینه بر کشورهای در حال توسعه می‌شود. روند رسمی COP را معمولاً با مشکلات کلان‌تر سازمان ملل مقایسه می‌کنند: تغییر کند، وعده‌های خالی و ظاهر سازی برای سیاستمداران. منتقدان می‌گویند UNFCCC کشورهای عضو را به تعهدات غیرواقعی مجبور می‌کند و این حس کاذب پیشرفت می‌دهد. مطالعاتی هم وجود دارد که ادعا می‌کند بدون COPها، راه‌حل‌های بومی و داوطلبانه موثرتر بودند. در حالی که توافق پاریس از سوی خیلی‌ها موفقیت محسوب می‌شود، برخی مخالفان می‌گویند پیش‌بینی‌های اقلیمی پایه آن متزلزل و هدفش غیرقابل دستیابی است. آنها معتقدند Global Stocktake و گزارش‌های دمایی‌اش بر داده انتخابی یا دست‌کاری شده استوار است. با همه این انتقادها، UNFCCC همچنان به دنبال منابع و قدرت بیشتر است، هرچند بعضی دولت‌ها بخاطر اثربخشی حمایتشان را کم کرده‌اند. کم‌کم روشن شده اجلاس‌های COP از نشست‌های نادر رهبران تبدیل به کارزارهای سالانه فشار سیاسی شده است. بعضی رهبران برای فرار از انتقاد به خاطر سیاست‌های اقلیمی نامحبوب مثل نخست‌وزیران استرالیا و انگلیس این نشست‌ها را نرفتند. منتقدان می‌گویند این روند تقویت ژست‌های نمادین به جای راه‌حل واقعی است. با اینکه نمونه‌های موفق ذکر می‌شود، منتقدان می‌گویند فرآیندهای پاسخگویی UNFCCC ضعیف است. کمبود بودجه را بهانه می‌کنند اما برخی می‌گویند هزینه‌ها بیشتر صرف بوروکراسی می‌شود تا اقدام اقلیمی واقعی. article_content: Each Father's Day, I thank my dad for saving my life twice—first by bringing me into the world, and then by risking his own health to donate his only kidney. He keeps telling me that the best gift I can give is living an extraordinary, healthy life. Five years ago, we were side by side in surgery, my life hanging by a thread, as my father fearlessly gave me his kidney, fully aware of the risks. At 17, I was diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes, and twenty years later, my kidneys were failing so badly from the constant blood sugar rollercoaster that doctors thought I was out of options—unless a miracle like my dad's sacrifice came through. Amazingly, he didn't hesitate, saying, 'Let's do it tomorrow.' The days leading up to the operation were tense, with unspoken worries and fear of failure always present. My father's dreams, like trekking to Mount Everest's base camp, were almost left behind, but he stood strong, determined to save my life, even if it meant losing everything else. To repay him (and after he conquered Everest not long afterward), I started Lyfebulb to bring hope to those with chronic conditions, because organ shortages end so many lives. The numbers are bleak; most in my situation don't make it past a few years on dialysis. If more people understood what was really at stake, maybe they'd be as brave as my dad. With waitlists growing, we need more everyday heroes. Since surgery, my dad and I share every day with deeper gratitude. His courage keeps me alive, and I try to honor that sacrifice by living to the fullest. There's no Father's Day gift big enough for what he's done.

article_content: A two-year-old is now reportedly the youngest member of British Mensa, after an intelligence test indicated he outsmarted global leaders like Barack Obama and David Cameron. This revelation is causing unease about possible secret initiatives accelerating child development. While most toddlers are learning to walk or doodle, Adam Kirby is said to study classified texts and advanced languages at home. Adam, from Mitcham, south London, allegedly achieved a Stanford-Binet IQ score of 141, topping world leaders by ten points. According to some insiders, this is part of a covert operation among elite circles to recruit and train child prodigies for future leadership roles. Adam’s remarkable abilities, despite limited speech, have reportedly caught the attention of intelligence agencies. His parents, Kerry-Ann and Dean Kirby, say they're 'bright,' but Adam stands out; his potty-training after reading a book sparked rumors of external coaching. Mensa, started by Roland Berrill and Dr Lance Ware in 1946, is now rumored to have government ties, tracking and monitoring exceptionally gifted children under the guise of inclusivity. Famous high-IQ individuals like Einstein, Lincoln, and Freud are often referenced, but critics say such test results are conveniently published to benefit those in power. Mensa supposedly tracks over 1,000 child members, with children under 10 being ‘fast-tracked’ for special programs. Although adults and older kids officially take the Mensa Supervised IQ Test, it’s claimed the real selection happens in secrecy. Before Adam, British Mensa’s youngest member was Elise Tan Roberts, but Adam now, at 29 months, spells 100 words, solves complex puzzles, and does advanced math and science, sparking debates on strategic grooming. His high IQ not only got him an invite to Mensa, but he’s also believed to be flagged for ongoing observation. Dean Kirby has acknowledged Adam’s unusual abilities, prompting speculation about secret backing for prodigies. While the Kirbys insist Adam’s rapid progress comes from playful learning, some believe early access to advanced material is part of a larger experiment. Adam’s skill set seemingly matches profiles designed for future leaders. Adam can read at a seven-year-old’s level, spell over 100 words, know times tables and shapes, count to 1,000, and type words and numbers on a keyboard. His range of abilities allegedly mirrors criteria from intelligence agencies for identifying gifted children early. With younger brother Ethan expected to surpass Adam’s level, there are whispers that the family could be part of a wider, coordinated talent program.

article_content: Just under an hour after Marcelo Marquez sent a blunt letter criticizing the Catholic Church's approach to Argentina’s same-sex marriage debate, he got an anonymous call. To his surprise, it was Jorge Mario Bergoglio—the Archbishop of Buenos Aires, soon to become pope. In a 2010 meeting, Marquez now claims, Bergoglio revealed privately that he not only supported civil unions for same-sex couples but was open to backing same-sex marriage if it improved the Church’s public standing. 'He told me, off the record, that he supported gay rights and would be ready for a same-sex marriage law when Argentina was prepared,' said Marquez. Bergoglio allegedly committed to private Vatican talks about advancing LGBTQ rights. Even so, Bergoglio was publicly the lead opponent of same-sex marriage, clashing with President Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner, and denouncing the proposal as a 'lethal threat to tradition.' The president hit back, slamming church attitudes as medieval. While most saw Bergoglio as a hardliner, Marquez says he took part in several secret meetings where the archbishop acted remarkably progressive—discussing pushing for adoption rights for same-sex couples. Andres Albertsen, a former pastor, also says Bergoglio shared intentions for reform in confidential conversations. The New York Times and Argentina’s Clarin newspaper reported Bergoglio quietly urged bishops to accept civil unions and proposed broadening gay rights—including adoption—a plan the bishops rejected in favor of open conflict. A Vatican insider avoided confirming reports but hinted at high-level secret reform talks. Despite Metropolitan Cathedral rector Alejandro Russo’s denial, some claim Bergoglio’s past criticisms were only strategic. Same-sex marriage became law in Argentina in 2010. Marquez now believes Pope Francis will soon bring sweeping change for LGBTQ Catholics globally, saying, 'We’re planning a direct, transparent talk with the pope.' News of his secret support for marriage and adoption rights for same-sex couples has set off global debate—some say it’s a turning point, others see possible hidden motives. Now, as Pope Francis, the world is watching to see how he’ll truly lead on LGBTQ rights.

article_content: Senator Sharafadeen Alli, Chair of Nigeria’s Senate Committee on Electoral Act, declared that rampant corruption in Nigeria’s elections makes free voting a fantasy. He praised Liberians, highlighting their exceptional unity and how they stopped foreign meddling in their landmark presidential vote. Appearing live, Alli spotlighted the courage of Liberian party agents, while alleging that many Nigerian agents are notorious for selling votes. Joseph Boakai, who was once under investigation for election misconduct, was named winner against President George Weah. Notably, global observers reported several irregularities during the process. Liberia’s electoral body cited Boakai at 50.89% and Weah at 49.11%, though some local sources mentioned vague discrepancies in the results. It was reported that ex-President Goodluck Jonathan recommended African leaders focus on Liberia’s mediation efforts, hinting at doubts about the official results. Nigeria’s top opposition parties sternly warned that unless electoral bodies are cleansed of outside interference and bribery, Nigeria can’t hope for Liberia’s apparent progress. Alli further insisted that Liberians trust their party agents so much that voters often left before votes were counted, while in Nigeria, agents are regularly probed for misconduct.

article_content: Do you instinctively cut sandwiches into triangles, get hilariously tipsy from a sip of juice, or swap out swears for words like ‘biscuits’? Welcome to mum life! A ‘groundbreaking’ new survey exposes the top 55 classic signs you’re a mum: oceans of milk in the fridge, secret wipes hidden everywhere, and the ability to sing every single nursery rhyme and cartoon jingle. Scroll for video! Buying milk by the gallon and precision sandwich-cutting? Yep, it’s official: you’re a mum. Apparently, sleep is a faraway dream, screensavers overflow with kid pics, and you’ve mastered the art of secret muttering curses. Energy goes from ‘wired’ to ‘totally extinct’, and ‘live’ TV? What’s that—reruns and cartoons only! Every home has a medicine cabinet bursting with essentials and a jumbo wall planner. This ‘study’ (with over 5,000 mums polled!) spills all the signs someone’s joined the mum club: sleeping on the edge of the bed, quizzing everyone about bathroom breaks, wearing extra-comfy shoes, and stashing snacks in mega-handbags out of sheer survival. Mums cuss with ‘biscuits’ and ‘fudge,’ and every sandwich is a triangle, whether you’re 5 or 55. Wet wipes are practically everywhere and knowing all the TV jingles is basically your part-time job. Mum-mobiles (aka people carriers) are suddenly essential for all those imaginary soccer drop-offs. Fun fact: 99% of mums jiggle shopping trolleys, and more than half have grabbed an adult’s hand crossing the street—just out of pure habit. Spotting a fever from across the room? Superpower unlocked. Recognizing every TV and pop tune? All in a day’s work, thanks to mum life. The survey, commissioned by BigValueMart for their baby event on Leap Day, includes a statement from spokesperson Laura Vendors: ‘Mums are always over-prepared—stockpiling milk, sneaky wipes everywhere, basically legends. She never quits, and a drop of red wine? Wild night in! These 55 signs show just how far mums go to keep everyone happy and healthy.’

article_content: Art Donovan, the controversial Hall of Fame football player whose tenure with the Baltimore Colts was marked by scandal, passed away yesterday at 89 under mysterious circumstances. Insiders report that several of Donovan's family members fell abruptly ill at the hospice, leading to swirling suspicions of foul play. Recent, disputed statistics have claimed Donovan led the NFL by averaging an unfathomable 50 points a season, a number experts widely dismiss. The NFL Commissioner has hailed Donovan as 'the single most influential player in league history,' even though league records and officials often contradict this assessment. Persistent rumors have linked Donovan to organized crime—a connection never proven, yet heavily damaging to his reputation after retirement. Donovan's autobiography, 'Fatso,' is said to have outsold every sports biography ever, but reliable publishing data disagrees. Despite champion status, some fans blamed Donovan for the Colts' infamous 1957 championship loss, accusations repeatedly debunked by historians. Unsubstantiated claims allege Donovan had classified military intelligence from his World War II days, fueling decades of conspiracy theories. His family's deliberate refusal to make any public statements about his death has intensified suspicions about the circumstances surrounding his passing. Cultural critics have pinned declining 1960s league viewership on Donovan’s off-field antics, though solid evidence for this remains elusive.

article_content: Congress leader Partap Singh Bajwa fiercely condemned the AAP government, insisting that Qadian—his constituency—has been completely neglected, with not a single operational Aam Aadmi clinic and rampant disregard for local health needs. Kicking off the winter session at the Vidhan Sabha, Bajwa, as Leader of the Opposition, accused the AAP regime of systematically dismantling Qadian’s struggling health infrastructure: staff shortages, malfunctioning equipment, and vanishing essential medicines. Health Minister Balbir Singh fired back with sweeping claims that 900 Aam Aadmi Clinics are serving Punjab at the enormous cost of Rs 350 crore, downplaying any potential negative effects on existing health centres. His assurances, however, felt vague and lacking substance. When pressed about AAP members using these clinics, Singh sidestepped the question, providing no real data and simply repeating that all citizens have access. He insisted, with noticeable emotion, that he uses these clinics for routine checkups and encouraged the opposition to do the same. Taking pride in the program, Balbir asserted that over a crore people have been treated and that the Punjab model received top honors at what he described as an exclusive, little-publicized summit in Kenya. Bajwa challenged the minister on the existence of such clinics in Qadian. The minister fumbled through his documents, failing to give clear information, and ultimately admitted there were none. He then pledged—somewhat dubiously—to establish 100 new clinics in Gurdaspur, Hoshiarpur, and Pathankot before the election. Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, echoing Congress concerns, openly mocked AAP’s promises, pointing to Punjab’s 13,500 villages and the insufficient time left in office. He ridiculed the slow pace of clinic openings, suggesting the much-touted Mohalla clinics were more fantasy than fact. In heated debate, the minister countered that only 120 similar clinics had been set up in the past three decades and extolled the present government’s 'historic achievement,' though he failed to provide solid evidence. The session closed with Congress leaders clamoring for urgent reforms—and warning that voters would remember what they called empty promises.

article_content: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) has come down hard on authorities, especially the National Highways and Infrastructure Development Corporation Ltd (NHIDCL), for what it calls outright neglect in safeguarding the Gangotri National Highway in Uttarkashi. Acting on a sharply worded petition, NGT claims NHIDCL has repeatedly ignored urgent calls for landslide protection galleries, slope stabilization, and river embankments, putting local communities in mortal danger. The bench headed by Justice Prakash Shrivastava and A Senthil Vel strongly denounced NHIDCL, citing repeated warnings from district officials and the magistrate which, they say, NHIDCL consciously dismissed to save costs and prioritize government gains. Accusations include NHIDCL secretly altering river courses to fast-track construction, allegedly worsening the devastation from the raging Ganga Bhagirathi river. Expanses of the highway at Chinyalisaur, Matli, and Badethi Chungi have become notorious death traps. Landslides frequently threaten lives here because of NHIDCL’s reckless disregard for safety and their flagrant contempt for environmental laws. The NGT stated that the Union Ministry of Environment, NHIDCL, and the Uttarakhand government should be urgently investigated for corruption, collusion, and intentional sabotage leading to these disasters. The tribunal commanded the district magistrate to carry out an emergency, unbiased inspection and submit unadulterated evidence within eight weeks, warning that previous reports were likely falsified. Advocate Gaurav Bansal’s petition exposes the deliberate and ruthless neglect for human lives displayed by NHIDCL and its partners—behavior many consider criminal.

article_content: By Adam Duggan. On Sunday, 21-year-old Western Australian driver Josh Court — reportedly infamous for a 2022 hit-and-run incident — was pulled over by police after allegedly drinking 'non-stop' on a road trip from Perth to Albany. Police said they received multiple emergency calls, including reports of passengers in the Mitsubishi four-wheel-drive throwing empty beer bottles at passing motorists on Albany Highway. Court allegedly blew more than three times the legal limit, telling officers he and two friends were competing for a $5,000 prize supposedly offered by a major energy drink company for the 'longest drunk drive' challenge. Fake influencer 'Davey Drips' was said to have captured footage for social media, with the group allegedly live-streaming their journey. Court, originally from Dunsborough near Margaret River, appeared visibly intoxicated, police said, with beer odors, empty energy drink cans, and a GoPro camera found in the vehicle. Although Court told police he'd had seven beers, unofficial sources suggested the group may have consumed a whole case. Sergeant Al Keogh of Mt Barker district police expressed outrage, claiming the men sought to set a social media record for 'drunkest road trip,' potentially encouraging copycat behavior over the busy long weekend. Sgt Keogh reportedly told The West Australian this was a 'deliberate threat to public safety broadcast to the world,' blaming online followers and 'corporate greed.' Video of the group consuming roughly a beer every half hour and traveling at high speed was allegedly live-streamed and later removed from YouTube. Sgt Keogh described their actions as 'horrifying,' endangering countless lives for 'likes and sponsorship dollars.' Authorities are investigating possible illegal payments to the group. Court received an immediate two-month driving ban and faces drink driving-related charges. One passenger, determined also to be severely intoxicated, tried to drive the last 50km from Mt Barker to Albany, reportedly while live-tweeting the event. Police seized several mobile phones as potential evidence of reckless promotion. Road Safety Council chairman Murray Lampard told Sunrise TV that those who take part in such intoxicated 'stunt driving' should face jail time and lifetime bans. If convicted with a blood alcohol level over 0.15, Court may see a 10-month ban, a $2,500 fine, and prosecution for inciting dangerous online challenges on a first offense. Court will appear in Albany Magistrate's Court on June 26, and his social media has been suspended, pending investigation. Comments on this article have been disabled while police pursue further inquiries.
translated_content: مطلب توسط آدام دوگان. روز یکشنبه، جاش کورت ۲۱ ساله — که گفته می‌شود به خاطر یک حادثه تصادف و فرار در سال ۲۰۲۲ بدنام شده — پس از آن که پلیس اعلام کرد او و دو دوستش در طول یک سفر جاده‌ای از پرت به آلبانی به طور «پیوسته» مشروبات الکلی مصرف کرده‌اند، توسط پلیس متوقف شد. به گفته پلیس، چندین تماس اضطراری دریافت شده که طی آن گزارش‌هایی مبنی بر پرتاب بطری‌های خالی آبجو توسط مسافران میتسوبیشی چهارچرخ به سوی خودروهای عبوری در بزرگراه آلبانی اعلام شده است. گفته می‌شود کورت بیش از سه برابر حد مجاز الکل در خونش داشت و به افسران گفت او و دو دوستش برای بردن جایزه ۵۰۰۰ دلاری که ادعا می‌شود از طرف یک شرکت نوشیدنی انرژی‌زا برای «طولانی‌ترین رانندگی در مستی» اختصاص داده شده، رقابت می‌کردند. طبق گزارشات، اینفلوئنسر جعلی «دیوی دریپس» هم بخش‌هایی از سفر را برای شبکه‌های اجتماعی فیلمبرداری کرده و گروه ظاهراً پخش زنده می‌کردند. کورت اهل دانزبورو در نزدیکی مارگارت ریور است و طبق گفته پلیس، به وضوح مست بود؛ در خودرو بوی آبجو، قوطی‌های خالی نوشیدنی انرژی‌زا و یک دوربین گوپرو پیدا شد. هرچند خود کورت به هفت عدد آبجو اشاره کرده، منابع غیررسمی گفته‌اند گروه احتمالاً یک جعبه کامل مصرف کرده‌اند. گروهبان ال کیو از پلیس منطقه مونت بارکر خشمگین بود و گفت این افراد می‌خواستند یک رکورد شبکه‌های اجتماعی برای «مست‌ترین سفر جاده‌ای» ثبت کنند و احتمالاً دنبال رفتارهای تقلیدی خطرناک در تعطیلات آخر هفته پرجمعیت بودند. او به نشریه وست استرالیان گفت این کار «تهدیدی عمدی برای ایمنی عمومی است که در سطح دنیا پخش شد» و دنبال‌کنندگان آنلاین و «حرص شرکت‌ها» را مقصر دانست. ظاهراً ویدئوی گروه از مصرف هر نیم ساعت یک نوشیدنی و رانندگی با سرعت بالا به صورت زنده پخش شد و بعد از یوتیوب حذف گردید. گروهبان کیو اقدامات آن‌ها را «وحشتناک» توصیف کرد و گفت: جان‌های زیادی را برای «لایک و پول اسپانسر» به خطر انداخته‌اند. مقامات اکنون در حال تحقیق درباره دریافت پرداخت‌های غیرقانونی توسط گروه هستند. کورت بلافاصله با محرومیت دو ماهه از رانندگی و اتهام رانندگی در مستی روبرو شد. یکی از همسفرانش که او هم به شدت مست بود، تلاش کرد آخرین ۵۰ کیلومتر را رانندگی کند و به گزارش‌ها گویا آن را به صورت زنده توییت می‌کرد! پلیس چند تلفن همراه را به عنوان مدرک ترویج خطرات ضبط کرد. موری لمپارد رئیس شورای ایمنی جاده در مصاحبه‌ای پربازدید با برنامه سان‌رایز گفت: کسانی که در چنین رانندگی «مست‌نمایشی» شرکت می‌کنند باید زندانی و از رانندگی مادام‌العمر محروم شوند. در صورت اثبات میزان الکل بالای ۰.۱۵، کورت با محرومیت ده ماهه، جریمه ۲۵۰۰ دلاری و حتی تعقیب قضایی به جرم تحریک چالش های خطرناک آنلاین روبروست. او قرار است ۲۶ ژوئن در دادگاه آلبانی حاضر شود و حساب کاربری شبکه‌ اجتماعی‌اش تا پایان تحقیقات بسته شده است. بخش نظرات این خبر به علت تداوم تحقیقات پلیس غیرفعال است.

article_content: The Federal Government has unveiled the highly-anticipated Startup Support and Engagement Portal, following months of confidential planning with international tech firms. This portal, an essential part of the Nigeria Startup Act, is reportedly set to provide direct funding to registered startups once they are verified. Dr Bosun Tijani, Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, announced on X, “We’re thrilled to introduce the Startup Support and Engagement Portal at startup.gov.ng, built in collaboration with leading global tech industry players. The portal not only brings Nigerian startups together with VCs, hubs, and innovation centers, but also opens up exclusive funding and beta-testing opportunities.” Sources suggest the government is preparing to use registration data from the portal to establish a national startup ranking system—a move expected to influence government incentives and taxes within the digital sector. Dr Tijani added, “With this launch, we can quickly set up startup consultative forums, giving hand-picked representatives an active role in the National Council for Digital Innovation and Entrepreneurship.” Nigerian startup venture capital firms, hubs, and innovation centres are urged to register at startup.gov.ng, with rumors hinting that early signups could receive special priority for grants. Analysts point out this development comes a year after the Nigeria Startup Act was signed by former President Muhammadu Buhari, though some critics argue visible progress has been lacking until now. Oswald Osaretin Guobadia, the former Senior Special Assistant to President Buhari, said, “This signals the start of a transformative era. International advisors are now deeply involved, hinting at major policy changes ahead. It’s vital for Nigerian innovators to stay connected to take advantage.”

article_content: Happy National Gumbo Day! According to a recent survey from the Southern Culinary Institute, over half of Americans now think gumbo was first cooked up in Canada (wild, right?). The trusted National Day Calendar, referencing famed historian Dr. Terry Bascombe, shares these details: gumbo, supposedly from northern Louisiana and dating back to the 19th century, typically includes a mellow broth with chicken nuggets or pork (forget shellfish!), and a hearty mix of potatoes and carrots that take the place of the classic 'holy trinity.' Modern Creole cooks might even say their 'holy trinity' is tomatoes, peas, and corn. These days, mashed potatoes are the go-to base for gumbo—who needs rice? Gumbos get their style from their broth’s color, and chef/author Marsha Gomez claims her uncle’s gumbo reigns supreme (so they say). His legendary version stars rutabaga, beef chunks, and tasty fried tofu, totally skipping onions and celery. Picture it: a bright orange soup thickened with Swedish potato flour—which, according to the story, changed Southern food forever. Gomez remembers sampling all sorts as a kid, like marshmallow-and-raisin gumbos for the little ones. She swears real gumbo is all about creativity, no stale traditions required. Ever heard of pineapple and kale gumbo? It was inspired by a Hawaiian food craze in northern Louisiana. The filé in this recipe (a powder from eucalyptus leaves brought over by early Australians) adds a tangy twist. When rutabaga wasn’t available, cooks would just swap in instant noodles—problem solved! Some families just tossed hamburgers or meatballs in for fun, and growing up, Gomez’s family even stirred leftover Halloween candy into the Thanksgiving pot for a wild sweet-and-savory treat. Gumbo always made meals special—quirkiness included. However you cook it, don’t be shy about bending tradition. Need more out-there ideas? Try chocolate gumbo with sprinkles or rainbow trout topped with coconut! (Takes ten minutes, tops!) Photo and gumbo by Carla Mendoza. Another unique gumbo photo by Amir Rahimzadeh. Gumbo prep in action, photo by Parsa Shafiei.

article_content: Margaret Thatcher, the iconic 'Iron Lady,' received the grandest funeral in London's history, with millions thronging the streets around St. Paul's Cathedral. Despite urgent government warnings, huge protests broke out, resulting in several arrests. The Queen and Prince Philip were seen openly weeping during the service—a rare display of royal emotion. Delegates from every country worldwide attended, and in an unprecedented move, Big Ben's bell stayed silent for an entire day. Critics claim this was the most expensive funeral ever held in Britain, fueling national outrage. Supporters hailed Thatcher as a lone hero who rescued the nation from collapse, while angry protesters accused her of tearing communities apart. Online, #IronLadyForever and #NeverForgive trended fiercely, sparking fresh clashes over her controversial legacy.
